title: Settings
tagline: Make it yours. None of this touches what Compy measures.

language.title: App language
language.sub: Changes every screen in Compy. English stays the default until you switch.

closeToTray.title: When I close, keep Compy running in the tray
closeToTray.sub: Off (default): closing fully quits Compy. On: closing tucks it into the system tray — you'll see the Compy icon there. Right-click it for Show or Quit; hover for live FPS while you play.

motion.title: Motion
motion.sub: Compy's living motion is on by default, even if Windows requests reduced motion. Choose Follow system to defer to Windows, or Reduced to keep everything calm.

homeInterview.title: Ask me a question on Home
homeInterview.sub: Home's main button opens a short interview — one plain question at a time — instead of just sitting there. Turn it off and Home shows the verdict and nothing else.

expertView.title: Expert view
expertView.sub: For tinkerers: shows every tweak's technical name and the exact registry key, service, or setting it touches, opens the "deliberately refused" list with full reasoning, and swaps rounded stats for raw measured values. Same tweaks, same limits — nothing new becomes appliable.

overlayDensity.title: In-game overlay density
overlayDensity.sub: What the in-game overlay shows: just FPS · + 1%/temp/GPU · + a frametime line.

overlayBackdrop.title: In-game overlay background
overlayBackdrop.sub: Off makes the overlay see-through — the numbers float on the game, outlined so they stay readable.

setup.title: Take the Compy tour again
setup.sub: Replay the tour, then run a fresh first check.

about.privacy: Runs on your PC. No account, no telemetry — nothing about your rig is ever uploaded. Compy's one outbound call is a signed update check, and you can turn it off.

updateChecks.title: Automatic update checks
updateChecks.sub: Checks a GitHub release page at launch and every 4 hours. Sends nothing about your PC. Turn this off and Compy makes no network request unless you press Check now.

feedback.hintPre: Hit a bug, have an idea, or just want to send what Compy sees on your PC? Write a note and Compy builds a diagnostic report for you.
feedback.hintPost: — "Email it to me" opens your own email app with everything filled in, and a copy is always saved on your PC either way.
feedback.notesPlaceholder: What's working, what's broken, or what you'd want next…
feedback.tierConsumerSub: What Compy changed, measured, and flagged — in plain words.
feedback.tierTechnicalSub: Hardware, checks, sessions, and diagnostics. Programs that start during a game are named only if Compy knows them, and your Windows user name is taken out of file paths.
feedback.errEmailFailed: Couldn't open your email app. Your report is saved below — you can attach it to an email yourself.
feedback.errBuildFailed: Couldn't build the report. Nothing was sent.
feedback.mailNoNote: (no note written — the saved report has the diagnostics)
feedback.mailTrimmed: …(trimmed — full text in the saved report)

supportEvidence.hintPre: A short rolling log of what Compy itself did — app starts, reads and writes of the Trust Ledger, the FPS capture helper starting and stopping, and whether each apply or rollback succeeded, failed, or was declined at the Windows admin prompt. It records outcomes, not content: no file contents, no keystrokes, no browsing, no game data. Usernames, your computer name, file paths, IP addresses, keys and serials are replaced with placeholders as it is written, and again when you export it.
supportEvidence.hintStrong: Compy has no way to upload it
supportEvidence.hintPost: — you read it here, save it to a file, and attach that file to a support conversation yourself.
supportEvidence.detailSub: The same records told three ways — pick what you're comfortable handing over.
supportEvidence.unreadable: {{n}} records couldn't be read and were left out.
supportEvidence.unreadableOne: 1 record couldn't be read and was left out.
supportEvidence.retention: Compy keeps the newest {{events}} records (about {{kb}} KB) and drops older ones as new ones arrive.
supportEvidence.clearWarn: Clearing it starts an empty record. If you later ask for help with something that already went wrong, there'd be nothing left to show — so clear it after a support conversation, not before.
supportEvidence.cleared: Cleared. Compy started a fresh, empty record.

yourData.header: What Compy keeps about your PC stays on this PC: its files are in %APPDATA%\Compy, and this window keeps a few notes of its own. Compy doesn't send any of it anywhere unless you send a report yourself.
yourData.playHistorySub: Deletes the play sessions Compy measured, the hardware and driver history it compares against, Trial results and crash notes. Your change history stays, so every change Compy made can still be undone. You see the full list before anything is deleted.
yourData.planChanged: Something in Compy's data changed since the last list, so nothing was deleted. This is the list as it is now.
yourData.nothingToDelete: There is no play history to delete right now.

store.drift: Notes on which checks were last as expected, and when that changed
store.crashNotes: Crash and freeze notes (Compy reads these from Windows' own logs, so it may note recent crashes again at its next check)
store.other: Other working files and damaged copies Compy made

yourData.webviewLine: Play-history notes this window keeps: the last check's result, a few counts, your Learn grading statistics, which care steps were shown, your helpful votes on crash notes, guided-journey state, your monitor's refresh rate, saved GPU settings snapshots and one-time screen hints
yourData.driftNotice: The check notes include any standing notice that a check Compy watches was found changed, and its 30-day record of settings found off and later read back on, with the names of the changes involved. Those go too; Compy starts watching again at its next check.
yourData.keptChangeHistory: Your change history and its backup: every change Compy made can still be undone. It names the settings Compy changed.
yourData.keptReports: Reports you saved stay in %APPDATA%\Compy\exports. They can hold session data, such as the games you played and how they ran, and the names of programs you ran. Delete them yourself if you want them gone.

kept.undo_data: A Gaming Mode file that may be needed to restore changes Gaming Mode made.
kept.trials_tied_to_changes: Trial results, because changes are still applied (or the change history can't be read) and the results are linked to them.
kept.trial_record_set_aside: A damaged copy of the Trial records: it may be the only record of a change a Trial made.
kept.elevated_leftover: A file an admin helper left behind: it is not play history and may show which steps of an earlier change finished.
kept.working_file_in_use: A working file less than an hour old: it may belong to something running.
kept.link_left_alone: A link or cloud placeholder: Compy doesn't follow it.
kept.clear_in_progress: The record of an earlier clear that is not finished.
kept.not_in_this_choice: Not play history: your support record, saved reports, dismissed items, sharing choice, licence and downloaded rule files. The support record and saved reports can name programs you ran.

yourData.unknownFiles: Files Compy didn't create, which it never deletes: {{files}}
yourData.legacyFolder: An older Sentinel folder exists at %APPDATA%\Sentinel. Compy doesn't touch it. It may hold older play history.
yourData.afterwards: After this, Compy needs a few normal sessions of each game before it can tell you what changed. It starts recording again from now on.
yourData.cantUndo: This can't be undone. Compy deletes these files directly, with no backup and not to the Recycle Bin.

refusal.capture_running: Compy is measuring a game right now. Close the game or stop measuring first.
refusal.recording_in_progress: Compy is still saving the play session it just measured. Try again in a moment.
refusal.benchmark_trial_running: A benchmark trial is running. Let it finish or cancel it first.
refusal.trial_running: A Trial is starting, running or was interrupted while starting, so a change it made may still be on. Let it finish or stop it first.
refusal.trial_state_unknown: Compy can't read its Trial records, so it can't tell whether a Trial change is still on. The file was left as it is.
refusal.gaming_mode_active: Gaming Mode is holding changes right now. End it first.
refusal.gaming_working_file: A Gaming Mode working file was left behind. It may belong to a session that did not finish, so Compy deletes nothing until it is dealt with.
refusal.root_unreadable: Compy couldn't read its data folder.
refusal.root_not_a_plain_folder: Compy's data folder is a link or not a folder, so Compy won't delete inside it.
refusal.data_root_unavailable: Compy isn't using its normal data folder right now, so it won't delete anything.
refusal.trials_tied_to_changes: A change was applied (or the change history can't be read) since the list was made, so the Trial results were kept: they are linked to it.
refusal.other: Compy can't clear right now (reason code {{code}}).

yourData.resultAllGone: Nothing was deleted: every listed file was already gone.
yourData.resultStopped: Stopped part way, because of what is listed below. Files deleted: {{n}}. Files not tried: {{left}}. Run it again afterwards.
yourData.resultNotFinished: Not finished. Files deleted: {{n}}. Files that could not be deleted: {{failed}}. Files not tried: {{left}}. Close whatever is using them and run it again.
yourData.fileFailedInUse: Could not delete: {{file}} (another program has it open)
yourData.fileFailedStillThere: Could not delete: {{file}} (it was still there after the delete)
yourData.fileFailedMoved: Could not delete: {{file}} (it is no longer the plain file Compy listed, so it was left alone)
yourData.fileFailedFolderMoved: Could not delete: {{file}} (a folder on its way is no longer the plain folder Compy listed, so nothing in it was touched)
yourData.webviewCleared: Play-history notes this window kept, also removed: {{n}}.
yourData.webviewLeft: These notes in this window could not be removed: {{keys}}
yourData.webviewNotTouched: The play-history notes this window keeps were not removed, because the clear did not finish.
yourData.crashNotesReturn: Compy reads crash notes from Windows' own logs, so recent crashes may show up again after its next check.
yourData.reloadNotice: This window still shows what it had loaded before. Reload it to start fresh, or close and reopen Compy.
yourData.restartOther: Compy still holds some of this in memory (reason codes {{codes}}). Close and reopen Compy to finish.
yourData.errPlan: Couldn't read what would be deleted. Nothing was deleted. {{detail}}
yourData.errClear: Compy couldn't finish clearing. Some files may already be deleted. Check again to see what is left. {{detail}}
